C H A P T E R V
IMPLEMENTATION OF SERVICES
First Part
Institutional

CHAPTER VI
ASSISTANCE
Article 11
Assistance is carried out by persons or institutions that have the expertise to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of victims of violence and have cooperated with P3A (Women and Children Service Center).

Article 7
(1) The Regent establishes a public service work unit that functions as a facilitator for the Women and Children Service Center (P3A).
(2) The P3A (Women and Children Service Center) as referred to in paragraph (1) in handling services and protection for women and children victims of violence may establish partnerships with social community institutions engaged in the field of services and protection for women and children.
(3) Provisions regarding the institutional structure of P3A (Women and Children Service Center) shall be further regulated by Regent Regulation.

Article 4
- What is meant by "obtaining protection" is obtaining protection from individuals, groups or institutions, both governmental and non-governmental.
- Obtaining information about the existence of complaint centers, P3A and matters related to the fulfillment of their rights and being involved in every decision-making process related to assistance and developments in case handling.
- What is meant by "integrated services" are services that include medical, medico-legal, psychosocial and legal.
- What is meant by "continuous handling" is handling that does not only stop at physical and psychological recovery, but until the victim can resume their life in society including restoration of their good name.

CHAPTER VIII
PROVISIONS ON SANCTIONS
Article 13
(1) Every person who intentionally fails to provide services and protection to women and children resulting in the occurrence of violence, allows violence to occur, and or fails to report and fails to provide protection to victims, shall be subject to sanctions as stipulated in the applicable laws and regulations.
(2) If Officials appointed to provide services and protection fail to carry out their obligations and responsibilities, they shall be subject to sanctions in accordance with the provisions of the applicable laws and regulations.
- 7 -

CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Regency Government is the Regency Government of Bojonegoro.
2. Regent is the Regent of Bojonegoro.
3. Child is a person who has not yet reached 18 years of age, including those in the womb.
4. Violence is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, economic, social, psychological to the victim.
5. Physical violence is any act that results in pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, fainting and or causes death.
6. Psychological violence is an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and or severe psychological suffering to a person.
7. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual relations, whether unnatural or unwanted with another person for commercial purposes and or certain purposes.
8. Economic violence is the neglect of family members in the form of not providing a proper standard of living care and maintenance.
9. Victim is a woman and child who experiences misery and or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence.
10. Services for Women and Children are actions that must be immediately taken including protection provided to victims when seeing, hearing and knowing of the impending, ongoing or completed occurrence of violence against victims.
11. Protection of women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the community, the police, the prosecutor's office, the courts, social institutions or other parties who know or hear of impending or completed violence against women.
12. Child protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
13. Companion is a person or representative from an institution who has the expertise to accompany victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of violence victims.
14. Women and Children Service Center hereinafter abbreviated as P3A is an institution providing services to victims of violence in the form of medical services (including medico-legal), psycho-social and legal services.
15. Safe house is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with determined operational standards.
16. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and or community organizations.
17. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband-wife, or husband-wife and their children, or father and his children, and mother and her children.
18. Household is family members and relatives (grandchildren, nieces/nephews, older siblings, younger siblings, grandfathers, grandmothers, cousins and so on) who live and eat from one kitchen and reside in one house.

NUMBER 10 YEAR 2011
CONCERNING
SERVICES FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN
VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE IN BOJONEGORO REGENCY
I. GENERAL ELUCIDATION
Services and protection for Women and Children constitute a series of activities that must be pursued continuously, sustainably, in a directed manner and guarantee the growth and development of children both physically, mentally, spiritually and socially so as to realize a good life and be able to become potential, resilient successors of the nation with noble character and possessing a strong sense of nationalism to maintain the unity and integrity of the nation and state. In addition, the Government also guarantees that the rights of women and children are fulfilled through Laws and Regulations that protect women and children from violence and discrimination. This is philosophically stated in the Preamble of the 1945 Constitution, that the first objective of the establishment of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia is to protect all the people and the entire homeland of Indonesia.

Therefore, the Indonesian Government has signed the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR) on December 10, 1948 and ratified CEDAW with Law Number 7 Year 1984 concerning the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women, thus is obliged to comply with these provisions. Likewise in the Amendment to the 1945 Constitution and Law Number 39 Year 1999 concerning Human Rights, it is stated that the enforcement and fulfillment of Human Rights is the responsibility of the state, especially the government, and the said Law also serves as a legal umbrella for all formation of Laws and Regulations that guarantee the realization and protection of women's human rights in implementing the elimination of discrimination.

Furthermore, in the National Action Plan for the Elimination of Violence Against Women of 1999, it is stated that women as mothers of the nation and children as the next generation of the nation who are creatures of God Almighty must therefore be protected and their honor, dignity and self-worth safeguarded in a reasonable and proportional manner both legally, economically, politically, socially and culturally without distinguishing ethnicity, religion, race and class.

- 2 - From the series of provisions above, the Government is responsible for taking actions both legally, politically, economically and socially to prevent, suppress, reduce and eliminate all forms of violence against women and children because this constitutes a crime against human existence.

Article 3
The purpose of services and protection for women and children victims of violence is to provide services and protection for women and children victims of violence that is based on gender and the best interests of the child that occurs in the household and or public.

II. ARTICLE-BY-ARTICLE EXPLANATION
Article 1
Services also include protection for women and children victims of violence

2.1.rationale: In the Indonesian source, the regulation establishes P3A and allows it to partner with community/social institutions (Pasal 7(2): "dapat melakukan kemitraan dengan lembaga-lembaga sosial kemasyarakatan...") and mentions protection activities can be carried out by multiple actors (Pasal 1(11): community, police, prosecutor, courts, social institutions, etc.). However, it does not set out an explicit institutional network/coordination mechanism across government jurisdictions (e.g., coordination with provincial/national agencies or other regencies) or a formal coordination structure/procedure; it is mainly an internal regency arrangement plus optional partnerships. The retrieved English passages accurately reflect this. Therefore the judge’s 'No' is consistent with the actual content, suggesting the golden 'Yes' label is likely incorrect for this indicator as defined (network/coordination mechanism).
